description: The plot illustrates how next-token prediction accuracy changes over training steps for two experiments, labeled “Ex1 Accuracy” and “Ex2 Accuracy.” The x-axis is labeled “Step,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 60,000 with regularly spaced tick labels every 10,000 steps. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (Next Token Prediction),” uses a linear scale, and shows values roughly from 0.10 up to about 0.42 with tick labels at approximately 0.05 intervals (e.g., 0.10, 0.15, …, 0.40). The Ex1 Accuracy series is a blue solid line with circular markers; it starts near 0.09 at step 0, rises to about 0.24 at 1,000 steps, increases to about 0.39 at 8,000 steps, and then gradually increases and flattens, reaching about 0.40 at 13,000, about 0.41 around 25,000–35,000, and ending near 0.41 at 60,000. The Ex2 Accuracy series is a teal solid line with circular markers; it starts near 0.09 at step 0, rises to about 0.27 at 1,000 steps, increases to about 0.28 at 8,000 and about 0.29 at 14,000, then jumps to about 0.36 at 19,000 and continues a gradual rise, reaching about 0.38 around 30,000–35,000 and ending near 0.39 at 60,000.
